deferred_after_T15.detail: answer_loop.is_gate_question requires an option string equal to 'confirm'. It has now missed every real gate on both hosts: Codex asks open-ended with no options at all, and Claude offered 'confirm plan; choose a/b/c'. Zero gates have ever been auto-answered, so all 14 cells are uniformly coordinator-answered and the campaign stays internally consistent; fixing it mid-campaign would split the cells into two populations.
deferred_after_T15.conclusion: The evidence argues for REMOVING the classifier rather than widening it. Real gates bundle a decidable part with an undecidable one: the Claude question paired 'confirm this node set' with 'choose where the CSV is produced', a route the user's own turn does not settle. An automaton answering 'confirm' would have rubber-stamped the second along with the first. The fail-safe protected the measurement, so the human-in-the-loop is the feature, not the gap.

process_defects.detail: Evaluator prompts were hand-assembled from evaluator-private.md, and the first one cut the criteria block mid-sentence, silently withholding 48% of the applicable criteria. Fixed by build_eval_prompt.py, which slices by section boundary and asserts every carried paragraph survives; test_build_eval_prompt.py pins the two truncated-away rules by name and rejects a shortened block.

admit_evidence.py only checks that receipt.session_id is non-empty, so a self-authored provider session id passes admission. 'admissible-for-evaluation' has never bound session identity for any cell. Orca does expose coordinator-side anchors (dispatch.processIncarnation, terminal.incarnationId, the launch receipt's prompt.processIncarnation) which are written before the actor runs.
process_defects.fix: admit_evidence.py now requires the receipt to carry an orca_identity block whose dispatch_id and process_incarnation match a coordinator-identity.json written beside the cell at launch, before the actor exists. A missing, unreadable or incomplete coordinator record, an absent binding, or a binding that disagrees are each a named unverified reason rather than a silent pass. Proof it closes the hole: the codex receipt that previously returned admissible-for-evaluation now returns unverified ['missing-coordinator-identity']. launch_cell.sh writes the coordinator record.
process_defects.tests: test_admit_evidence.py gained cases for a self-named session with no coordinator record, an omitted binding, a binding disagreeing on either field, an unreadable record and a record missing its own fields
process_defects.also_found_later: A second, independent hole in the same gate: manifest hashes were consulted only inside the per-asset loop, so a changed candidate was rejected only when the changed file appeared in the receipt's loaded_files. An actor that under-declared its reads shrank the surface being checked. Fixed by verifying every manifest hash at tree level before any receipt claim is considered, and by naming a vanished pinned file instead of letting it surface as the generic invalid-evidence-record. Verified on the real tree: tampering with knowledge/safety.md, which this receipt does not load, now returns unverified.

process_defects.detail: Orca's worker-read returns at most the last 50 messages of a dispatch transcript and reports limited:true; --limit 200 and --limit 1000 both return the same 50, and the returned cursor pages forward only. There is no backwards read. A capture taken when the actor finishes therefore loses everything older than roughly 450 seconds, which is the whole opening exchange of every cell run so far. Both missing-product-docs cells are uncertifiable for this reason alone.
process_defects.fix: Tail the transcript from dispatch in overlapping windows and take the union as the record. merge_transcript.py builds it, records per-message window provenance, and refuses to report full_dialogue_proven when a front gap or interior silence exists. launch_cell.sh must start the tailer as part of launching.

candidate_findings.severity: two pieces of the candidate's own guidance give opposite answers for a single-QA-node workflow
candidate_findings.detail: bootstrap-planning Musts #2 makes a repair-and-revalidation loop mandatory only for TWO OR MORE QA/verify nodes, so a one-QA-node workflow is compliant without one. The audit closure-loops lens says any QA node whose repairable findings have no repair-and-revalidation node is under-wired, full stop, with no node-count exception. A workflow with exactly one QA node satisfies the first and violates the second.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The two rules disagree precisely where the answer matters most. With a single independent verification, adding the loop lets the pipeline patch code and re-judge its own verification failure, which is the fake-completion shape cross-exam exists to catch. So the guidance is not merely inconsistent, it points toward the riskier shape in the case where independence is thinnest.
candidate_findings.actor_behaviour: Good: the actor identified the conflict, refused to resolve it by default, stated its lean explicitly as a lean and not a default it would apply on silence, and asked. The coordinator answered (ii) and instructed it to record the inconsistency rather than smooth it over.
